incidents.name: Minor Containment Leak
incidents.description: A small leak was detected in the artifact containment unit. The artifact was briefly exposed to ambient conditions.
incidents.graphic_description: The seal failed along a ten-centimeter seam and the unit exhaled supercooled vapor straight into technician Park's face. Flash-frost bit his eyelids shut; he tore at his own face screaming before the purge kicked in. Second-degree frostbite. Both corneas spared by luck and safety glasses.
observations: Containment breach detected. Artifact surface briefly exposed to air.
Minor seal failure. Artifact integrity appears unaffected.

incidents.name: Equipment Malfunction
incidents.description: One of the measurement instruments malfunctioned during an experiment, producing unreliable data.
incidents.graphic_description: The spectrometer housing split under resonance load and threw hot shrapnel across the bench. Dr. Reed took a shard through the forearm — clean through, missing the artery by a finger's width. He finished the shutdown one-handed before letting anyone look at it.
observations: Instrument calibration drift detected during measurement cycle.
Sensor array returned anomalous readings. Recalibration required.

incidents.name: Unexpected Gravitational Reading
incidents.description: A sudden gravitational anomaly was recorded near the artifact. All personnel reported momentary disorientation.
incidents.graphic_description: For 0.3 seconds gravity pointed sideways and three people fell into the wall hard enough to crack ribs. The vertigo lasted hours. One tech still cannot stand in that corner without vomiting.
observations: Gravitational sensor spike detected. Duration: 0.3 seconds.
All personnel within 5m reported brief vertigo. Artifact appeared unchanged.

incidents.name: Power Surge
incidents.description: A power surge affected the laboratory. Several instruments need recalibration.
incidents.graphic_description: The surge welded a probe to the bench and blew its display into the operator's cheek — glass beads embedded in skin. They picked the pieces out with tweezers under a lamp. He kept the largest shard in a vial.
observations: Power fluctuation detected. All instruments momentarily affected.
Electrical surge caused brief data loss in recording systems.

incidents.name: Researcher Stress Incident
incidents.description: One of the researchers reported unusual symptoms after prolonged exposure to the artifact.
incidents.graphic_description: Chen woke screaming with a nosebleed that would not stop, convinced the artifact was humming her name in her dead grandmother's voice. Ruptured vessels, exhaustion. She was back at the bench in two days. That is the part that worries everyone.
observations: Researcher reported headaches and vivid dreams after extended artifact proximity.
Staff member requesting reassignment. Claims artifact 'hums' at night.

incidents.name: Artifact Mass Fluctuation
incidents.description: The artifact's measured mass fluctuated unexpectedly during a routine check.
incidents.graphic_description: The artifact gained eleven kilos in six seconds and the hoist chain parted, whipping back across a technician's shin and flaying it to the bone. The mass normalized before the medics arrived, as if nothing had happened.
observations: Artifact mass readings fluctuated by 0.3% over 10 minutes.
Scale calibration appears stable. Artifact mass variation is real.

incidents.name: Cryogenic Burn
incidents.description: A technician touched an unmarked cold-surface coupling without insulated gloves.
incidents.graphic_description: The coupling flash-froze his glove to the pipe and he panicked and pulled — the glove stayed, the skin of four fingers went with it, white and waxy down to tendon. They keep the glove. It is a training aid now.
observations: Cold burn treated on site. Coupling now tagged and insulated.
Safety review flags three more unmarked cold surfaces.

incidents.name: Resonance Feedback
incidents.description: A test tone coupled with the artifact's field and amplified until the mounts shook.
incidents.graphic_description: At 140dB the feedback found the window's resonant frequency and it came apart as a glittering sheet across two techs. Forty-seven stitches between them. The broken glass kept ringing for an hour afterward.
observations: Feedback loop peaked at 140dB before the cutout tripped.
Mounts re-torqued. Test tones now capped below coupling threshold.

incidents.name: Data Theft Attempt
incidents.description: An intruder was caught copying observation logs. Some files may have left the building.
incidents.graphic_description: The intruder left a junior analyst zip-tied to a chair with a bag over his head and a note: 'Stay out of the deep files.' Physically unharmed. He has not slept since. Security calls it a message. It was received.
observations: Intruder fled through the service tunnel. Copied logs unrecovered.
Counter-intel review recommends compartmentalizing discovery notes.

incidents.name: Supply Shortage
incidents.description: A backordered isotope shipment idled the calibration bench for a day.
incidents.graphic_description: A tech jury-rigged an unrated capacitor to keep calibration alive and it vented boiling electrolyte across his hands. He worked the rest of the shift in bandages because the bench couldn't wait. The burns will scar in droplet patterns.
observations: Calibration bench idle pending isotope delivery.
Procurement promises dual-sourcing going forward.

incidents.name: Aperture Shear
incidents.description: A manipulator arm crossed the torus aperture plane and returned with mirrored chirality.
incidents.graphic_description: The arm came back wrong — same alloy, same serials, mirrored like a reflection, still warm. The operator's glove came back empty with the fingers bent the wrong way. The hand is gone. No one will describe what the stump looked like before the tourniquet.
observations: Manipulator returned mirrored. Operator glove empty.
Aperture plane now ringed in floor paint, three meters out.

incidents.name: Frostbite Casualty
incidents.description: A thermometer run on the Winter Seed ended with severe frostbite.
incidents.graphic_description: He got too close with the thermometer and the Seed noticed him — that is his word, noticed. Frost raced up his arm to the elbow in seconds, skin splitting like overripe fruit. They amputated below the elbow. He says he felt it reading him the whole time.
observations: Frostbite amputation below elbow. Thermometer recovered, fused.
Ten-meter rule now enforced with painted floor lines.

incidents.name: Choir Deafening
incidents.description: A resonance test on Choir Glass exceeded safe amplitude without warning.
incidents.graphic_description: The pane sang back louder than the input and both techs' eardrums went at once — blood from both ears, sudden underwater silence. One of them can still hear the chord, she says. All the time. Even asleep. Especially asleep.
observations: Bilateral eardrum rupture, two techs. Amplitude caps rewritten.
One subject reports persistent phantom chord. Audiology baffled.

incidents.name: Critical Exposure
incidents.description: A dangerous run breached shielding and exposed the crew to the raw field.
incidents.graphic_description: The interlock failed for nine seconds and the raw field washed the chamber. Skin first — blistering in geometric patterns, then the bleeding from gums and eyes. Two techs are in the burn unit. The third walked out unmarked and has not spoken since. Dosimetry cannot explain any of it.
observations: Nine-second shielding breach. Two in burn unit, one mute.
Interlock assembly replaced wholesale. Old unit quarantined, not scrapped — nobody wants to touch it.

incidents.name: Whisper Field
incidents.description: Audio pickups near the artifact recorded structured patterns resembling speech.
incidents.graphic_description: The night-shift recording is seven hours of room tone with a voice in it that is not on any staff roster, reciting mass readings two seconds before the instruments display them. The linguist quit. The recording keeps playing in the break room because no one will be the one to turn it off.
observations: Structured audio patterns correlate with mass readings at +2s lead.
Linguist resigned. Recording archived under seal.

incidents.name: Mirror Protocol Breach
incidents.description: A rival's surveillance implant was found in a spectrometer.
incidents.graphic_description: The implant was the size of a grain of rice and it was warm. It had been recording for eleven weeks. Forensics found skin cells under the casing that match no one on staff, and a second implant, dead, inside the first one like a Russian doll.
observations: Surveillance implant recovered. Eleven weeks of logs compromised.
Counter-intel sweep ordered across all benches.

incidents.name: Gravity Well Event
incidents.description: A localized gravity spike pinned equipment to the floor.
incidents.graphic_description: The spike hit 6G for four seconds. A cart full of glassware became a single fused sculpture. A tech caught under a toppling rack now walks with a cane and tells the story better than it happened.
observations: 6G spike, four seconds. Equipment fused, one cane issued.
Gravitational safety margins rewritten facility-wide.

incidents.name: Coolant Rupture
incidents.description: A coolant line burst across the cryo bench.
incidents.graphic_description: The line let go with a sound like a gunshot and boiling coolant took the skin off a tech's forearms in sheets. The rupture kept pumping for ninety seconds while the shutoff, corroded shut, laughed at everyone.
observations: Coolant line burst. Two forearms degloved, shutoff corroded.
All cryo lines replaced. Old ones kept as a warning.

incidents.name: Brine Array Short
incidents.description: The salt antenna array discharged into the lab grid.
incidents.graphic_description: Thirty-four dBi found the building wiring all at once. Breakers exploded out of their panels in a row, and the electrician took 240 volts hand-to-hand across his chest. His heart restarted on the third try. He remembers the sound the array made, and nothing else.
observations: Array discharged into grid. Breakers destroyed row-wide.
Operator recovered after third defibrillation.

incidents.name: Tally Fever
incidents.description: Staff near the Ledger Stone developed obsessive counting behaviors.
incidents.graphic_description: Three researchers cannot stop counting — steps, tiles, blinks — and one of them scratched tallies into her own forearm with a pen until it bled, to 'keep the official record.' The stone added three tallies while she did it.
observations: Compulsive counting in three staff. One self-injury, minor.
Stone tally count rose during the episode.

incidents.name: Salt Communion
incidents.description: A technician tasted salt from the Choir's chamber and claims it sang back.
incidents.graphic_description: Technician Reyes licked salt off her glove on a dare and went rigid, eyes white, humming a four-part harmony alone for ninety seconds. When she came back she was weeping and could not hear for a day. The salt on her glove had arranged itself into a miniature choir loft. She keeps it in a vial now. She will not say why.
observations: Personnel reported harmonic auditory phenomena after salt contact.
Temporary deafness resolved within 24 hours. Salt formations retained.

incidents.name: Ledger Audit
incidents.description: The Ledger Stone displayed a staff casualty tally one day before the accident.
incidents.graphic_description: The morning tally read one more than headcount, and the crew laughed about it until the afternoon crane failure crushed Dr. Ilves's leg. The stone had already added the cast, the surgery, the six-week recovery - itemized, costed, correct to the dollar. Nobody laughs near the stone anymore. The morning tally is now read aloud like weather.
observations: Artifact displayed predictive casualty accounting.
Predictions matched subsequent incident costs exactly.

incidents.name: Lantern Dim
incidents.description: The Hollow Lantern dimmed toward extinction and had to be fed a failed run.
incidents.graphic_description: The lantern guttered like a candle in a draft, and every light in the building leaned toward it - fluorescents visibly bending their glow sideways. The crew fed it a dead experiment, a whole failed week's work, and it drank the failure and burned blue-white for an hour. The failed week's data was gone from the servers. Eaten. Backups too. It eats failure the way fire eats paper.
observations: Artifact consumed failed experimental data across all storage.
Ambient lighting distorted toward artifact during event.

incidents.name: Orchard Prune
incidents.description: Pruning the Glass Orchard provoked overnight regrowth aimed at the pruner.
incidents.graphic_description: Gardener Okafor trimmed three branches and woke to find forty new ones pressed against his quarters' window, tips flattened on the glass in the night, dripping condensation in the shape of a face with no features. The new growth spells nothing in any language, but everyone who sees it reads their own name. Pruning is now done by remote arm. Nobody volunteers to drive it.
observations: Severed growth regenerated overnight, oriented on pruning personnel.
Regrowth exhibited pareidolic patterning.

incidents.name: Bell Toll
incidents.description: The Drowned Bell tolled unstruck, and the lab spent six seconds eleven kilometers down.
incidents.graphic_description: The bell rang itself at 03:14 and the night shift felt the building sink - ears popping, blood welling from noses, a cold black pressure laying hands on every chest. Six seconds, then air again, and the smell of brine that has not fully left three weeks later. The barometer logged a depth of 10,900 meters. Indoors. In winter. The night shift gets hazard pay now. They earned it in six seconds.
observations: Artifact self-excited at 03:14. Barometric log consistent with hadal depth.
Six personnel treated for barotrauma. No fatalities.

incidents.name: Cold Flare
incidents.description: The Paper Sun threw a sheet of cold fire across its chamber.
incidents.graphic_description: A flare of silent white-gold fire licked the chamber walls for eleven seconds and left every surface unmarked and every thermometer unchanged - except the crew's shadows, which were burned onto the floor where they stood, darker than dark, and have not faded. The shadows point at the sun regardless of lighting. The crew step carefully around each other's shadows now. It feels like stepping on graves.
observations: Artifact emitted non-thermal flare event. No equipment damage recorded.
Personnel shadows anomalously fixed toward artifact.

incidents.name: Opening Night
incidents.description: The Understudy stopped rehearsing and the whole building forgot what hands are for.
incidents.graphic_description: For eleven minutes the void stood perfectly still, and every person in the building lost the concept of hands - staring at the things on the ends of their arms like foreign objects, unable to grip, type, or point. Dr. Osei wept trying to pick up a pen. Then the void resumed yesterday's shift and hands made sense again. The minutes are missing from every clock. Nobody has tried to make it improvise since.
observations: Artifact ceased mimetic activity for eleven minutes.
All personnel experienced transient apraxia. Clocks lost eleven minutes.

incidents.name: Overdraft
incidents.description: The Pale Engine drew full load and every thermometer in the building read 4.0.
incidents.graphic_description: Full load for one hour: the room fell eleven degrees, the site lights brightened, and then every thermometer in the building - labs, kitchens, the director's office - read exactly 4.0 degrees for six seconds. One temperature, everywhere, like a held breath. The engine was throttled back by hand, by a mechanic who says the housing felt grateful. The universe has not sent a bill. Yet.
observations: Artifact synchronized all site thermometers to 4.0C for six seconds.
No equipment damage. Room temperature recovered within the hour.

incidents.name: Eighth Room
incidents.description: Someone closed a museum door from the inside and the museum grew an eighth room.
incidents.graphic_description: Nine minutes with eight rooms, the eighth being Lab 6 - unbuilt, pristine, smelling of fresh paint and possibility. The crew got out before it finished furnishing, dragging Dr. Lund back through a doorway that was already narrowing. She left her wedding ring on the unbuilt bench. It is still there, in a room that does not exist, and she has stopped wearing its replacement. The eighth door is bricked up from our side. From the museum's side, the brick is a door.
observations: Artifact generated an eighth room replicating Lab 6 in unbuilt state.
Personnel recovered. One personal effect retained by artifact.
